palette.notes: Measured 5 colours on one still, one ramp with no hue shift: black line, white fill, grey shading, pink blush, plus one blue reserved for the tear. Flipnote-style doodle made in a pixel app (Resprite), not classic shaded pixel art.

lighting: No lighting; flat white fills with a single grey shadow tone under the eye and chin of the big face.
silhouette: Two reads: a long row of tiny spiky white creatures with blush (a chain of identical heads), then a big outlined bald face in profile staring at that row; both read instantly as black line on white.

motion.timing: Measured median hold 100 ms (p25 67, p75 100), about 10.6 drawings/s, on 3s; TikTok copy so holds are rough. The joke lands through held reaction poses, not smooth motion.

texture: Wobbly hand-drawn line boil on a pure white page; no dither (share 0.0006).
camera: Static framing; one hard cut from the wide strip of creatures to a close-up of the face with the creatures shrunk into the background.

acting.enters: The creature row is already there; one creature opens its mouth in a black O and the cry passes down the line.
acting.acts: The cry repeats; the cut shows a big face listening, eye twitching, then crying a blue tear stream that grows each beat.
acting.exits: No exit; the face just breaks down more as the noise keeps coming.
acting.depth: The creatures move from full-frame hero to a tiny strip behind the face, so the cause stays visible small in the background while the reaction plays big in front.

techniques: repeat-and-escalate: the same small sound gag retriggers while the reaction grows
cut from cause (wide) to reaction (close-up) with the cause kept tiny in the background
one accent colour (blue tear) saved for the punchline in an otherwise black-white palette
drawn on 3s with line boil so even holds feel alive
feel: black line on white + 1 accent colour + small cause in back, big reaction in front = instant relatable meme
for_fred: Use the cause-small, reaction-big staging: Pixie keeps doing an annoying thing tiny in the background while Fred, close in front, reacts a bit worse on each repeat (eye twitch, then a single-colour tear). Hold each reaction pose 3 frames or more instead of animating everything.
